title: Skill invocations should be attributable transformations on document-model state
content:
## Claim

Model each skill invocation as an attributable transformation: an action against a document, dispatched by an attributed actor, executed by a deterministic reducer, and recorded in an append-only operation log.

## Implications

- State derives only from replaying the log
- Every byte in the final state traces to an operation → skill → actor
- The artifact and the provenance record are the same structure

## Contrast

Tool-call traces that live *beside* the artifact force post-hoc reconciliation. Unifying them ("the artifact is the log") removes that gap.

## See also (reweave)

- Related evaluation stance: process-level evaluation beyond output scoring
- Related memory risk: untyped knowledge-layer contamination modes
- Implementation conventions: three conventions for attributable skills


## Methodology grounding
The claims below live in the plugin's `data/methodology/` corpus; the relationship is stated per claim.

- **[[hook enforcement guarantees quality while instruction enforcement merely suggests it]]** — BUILDS_ON. A skill described in an instruction file is a suggestion; a skill invocation recorded as an operation on document state is enforcement, because the record exists whether or not the agent cooperated.
- **[[agents are simultaneously methodology executors and subjects creating a unique trust asymmetry]]** — RELATES_TO. Attribution is the asymmetry's remedy: if every transformation names its actor and its inputs, the agent's dual role stops being invisible to whoever audits the result.
description: Each skill call should be a typed, signed, replayable operation on known state, not an ephemeral tool invocation beside the artifact.
